transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm just so exhausted and depressed, and I've lost all motivation to do anything lately. My thoughts... they don't stick together anymore, they just drift apart like clouds and nothing connects. It's hard to even speak because the words get so
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt the opposite of this—having unusually high energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling on top of the world?
No, I've never had times like that at all. I have never experienced periods of high energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling on top of the world. It is always the complete opposite for me.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that others couldn't see, or felt like people were watching or plotting against you?

Yes, actually... it's been really terrifying lately. I keep hearing these quiet whispers when I'm completely alone in my room, and sometimes I see dark shadows moving out of the corner of my eye. I also can't shake this constant, heavy feeling that I'm being watched and monitored by people I can't see.
Have these experiences of hearing whispers or feeling watched ever happened during times when you weren't feeling depressed?

Yes, that has happened. There were times, lasting for a few weeks or even longer, where my mood actually felt okay and I wasn't feeling depressed. But even during those better weeks, the whispers and the feeling of being watched were still there.

Looking back over the entire time you've had these struggles, would you say the periods of severe depression have been present for most of that time, or have they been relatively brief compared to the whispers and feeling watched?

Yes, the severe depression has definitely been present for the vast majority of the time I've been struggling. The brief moments where I don't feel completely weighed down are very rare. It really feels like this heavy darkness has been there for almost the entire two and a half years.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ['Schizophrenia', 'Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)']. The patient reports experiencing psychotic symptoms (whispers, feeling watched) for weeks at a time when they were not depressed, ruling out Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features. Furthermore, the patient states that severe depression has been present for the vast majority of the total duration of their illness (almost the entire 2.5 years), which meets the criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) rather than Schizophrenia. Since there is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, we can confidently diagnose Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type).
